# `particle_voice/nn/memory/WeightResidencyPlan.js`

> **Source:** `agi/particle_voice/nn/memory/WeightResidencyPlan.js`

WeightResidencyPlan.js — Phase 1 ParticleNN memory. For each program segment (from a `PRNN-v0.md` §7 bind-window directory: `{ windows: [{ segmentId, pageIndices, bindGroupLayoutHash }] }`), which pages must be resident — plus the diff between two segments' page sets, so a scheduler can decide exactly which pages to load/evict when moving from one segment to the next instead of reloading everything.

## Classes

### `class WeightResidencyPlan`

WeightResidencyPlan.js — Phase 1 ParticleNN memory. For each program segment (from a `PRNN-v0.md` §7 bind-window directory: `{ windows: [{ segmentId, pageIndices, bindGroupLayoutHash }] }`), which pages must be resident — plus the diff between two segments' page sets, so a scheduler can decide exactly which pages to load/evict when moving from one segment to the next instead of reloading everything.

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(bindWindowDirectory)` |  |
| `segmentIds` | `segmentIds()` |  |
| `pagesForSegment` | `pagesForSegment(segmentId)` |  |
| `pagesForSegments` | `pagesForSegments(segmentIds)` | Union of pages required across several segments (e.g. a lookahead window of upcoming segments). |
| `diff` | `diff(fromSegmentIds, toSegmentIds)` | Moving from `fromSegmentIds` (currently resident, may be empty) to `toSegmentIds` (about to run): which pages can be evicted (no longer needed) and which must be loaded (not yet resident). |
| `totalDistinctPages` | `totalDistinctPages()` | Total distinct pages referenced anywhere in the plan — an upper bound on VRAM if everything were resident simultaneously (it never should be, per the plan's residency-window design). |

## Notes & Examples

### Where this fits in the training loop

AGI runs an **observation → brain → action → reward** loop each tick: observations are gathered from the world, a brain maps them to actions, the rig applies motion, and rewards shape the next update.

**Example: Minimal training loop**
```js
import { Agent } from 'agi/core/Agent.js';
import { World } from 'agi/env/World.js';

const world = new World();
const agent = new Agent({
  brain: 'ppo',
  observationSpace: world.observationSpace,
  actionSpace: world.actionSpace
});

for (let step = 0; step < 10000; step++) {
  const obs = world.getObservation();      // Gather observations
  const action = agent.act(obs);            // Brain decides action
  const { reward, done } = world.step(action); // Apply action, get reward
  agent.learn(obs, action, reward);         // Update from experience
  
  if (done) world.reset();
}
```

**See also:** [AGI Training Guide](/agi/training-guide.md) · [AGI Architecture](/agi/architecture.md)
